name: aspect-ratio
title: Aspect Ratio
description: Images, videos, and embeds that must keep their shape.
docs:
## Installation ```install npx shadcn@latest add @cadence/aspect-ratio ``` ## Usage ```tsx import { AspectRatio } from "@/components/cadence/aspect-ratio"; export function Cover() { return ( ); } ``` ## Square Use a ratio of `1` for a square crop. The image fills the reserved frame with `object-cover`; the ratio box owns layout, while the child owns its crop and accessible name. This self-contained illustration can be replaced by your own image. ```tsx "use client"; import { AspectRatio } from "@/components/cadence/aspect-ratio"; export function SquareImage() { return (
); } ``` ## Video A `16 / 9` frame reserves room for video before it loads. Native controls belong to the media itself and stay usable; there is no autoplay. This silent sample loads from MDN only when requested. Replace its source with your own clip and supply captions when it contains speech. ```tsx "use client"; import { AspectRatio } from "@/components/cadence/aspect-ratio"; export function VideoFrame() { return (
); } ``` ## Multiple ratios in one grid `ratio` accepts a positive numeric width divided by height, rather than a finite list of variants. Here `4 / 3`, `1`, and `3 / 4` reserve different shapes at the same column width. The parent chooses columns and narrow-screen wrapping; media loading does not determine the frame heights. ```tsx "use client"; import { AspectRatio } from "@/components/cadence/aspect-ratio"; export function RatioGrid() { const image = "data:image/svg+xml,%3Csvg xmlns=%22http://www.w3.org/2000/svg%22 viewBox=%220 0 320 240%22%3E%3Crect width=%22320%22 height=%22240%22 fill=%22%23334155%22/%3E%3Ccircle cx=%22240%22 cy=%2264%22 r=%2228%22 fill=%22%23fbbf24%22/%3E%3Cpath d=%22M0 240V180L100 80L240 240ZM120 240L240 120L320 200V240Z%22 fill=%22%2394a3b8%22/%3E%3C/svg%3E"; return (
{[{ ratio: 4 / 3, label: "4 : 3" }, { ratio: 1, label: "1 : 1" }, { ratio: 3 / 4, label: "3 : 4" }].map(({ ratio, label }) => ( ))}
); } ``` ## When to use - An image, video, or embed whose intrinsic size is unknown until it loads. - A thumbnail grid that must not reflow as the images arrive. - A placeholder that will be replaced by media of a known shape. ## When not to use - Fixed-size icons or avatars; give them a size and be done. - Text blocks. A ratio box around text clips exactly the content that needs to grow. - A container whose height should follow its content — that is a normal block. ## API | Prop | Type | Default | Description | | ----------- | -------- | ------- | ------------------------------------------------------ | | `ratio` | `number` | – | Width ÷ height. Required — there is no sensible default. | | `className` | `string` | – | Merged last; `overflow-hidden` and the radius go here. | The ratio is written as `--ratio`, and the box uses `aspect-(--ratio)`. Your own `style` is preserved: the custom property is merged after it. ## Motion contract No motion (T0). The whole point of the box is that it does not change size; a transition here would reintroduce the layout shift it exists to prevent. | Phase | Properties | Token | Interruptible | | ------- | ---------- | ----- | ------------- | | – | none | – | – | | reduced | none | – | – | | none | none | – | – | ## Accessibility - The box is a layout element with no role. Put the meaning on the media: a real `alt` on images, a `title` on iframes. - A background-only ratio box (no media yet) is decorative — keep it empty, or give it `aria-hidden` if it would otherwise be an empty accessible node. - Media that animates (autoplay video, GIF) counts against both the CLS budget and the reduced-motion contract; pause or replace it under `prefers-reduced-motion`. ## Responsiveness and performance The frame derives height from its available width and ratio. Give it a constrained parent and size media to fill the frame; the caller owns breakpoint-specific ratios and image loading. T0 adds no authored animation runtime or interpolation. This wrapper renders HTML/CSS; interactive children and application handlers still need their own client code. Server-rendered markup does not imply that every interaction works without JavaScript. The registry enforces a 4 KiB gzip budget for this item's own shipped source; dependencies and application bundles are measured separately. ## Notes for AI - Always pass a `ratio`; `16 / 9` for video, `1` for avatars, `4 / 3` for photos. - Put `object-cover` on the child, not on the ratio box. The box only reserves space; the child fills it.
